newsitem.title: USA: UN to tell Iranians to stop smuggling of Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: UN to tell Iranians to stop smuggling of Iraqi oil.

text.p: The United Nations Sanctions Committee on Iraq, responding to U.S. complaints made in August, plans to tell the Iranian government to stop illegal shipments of Iraqi gas oil through Iranian waters, according to a western diplomat on the panel.

After a meeting of the sanctions panel, it was decided to have chairman Tono Eitel of Germany write a letter to the Iranian leadership stating that "'there are violations taking place' and encourage Iran to do something about it," according to the diplomat.
The letter will not directly implicate the Iranian government in the alleged smuggling.

The smuggling charges originated in August when the United States accused Iran of allowing ships carrying illegal Iraqi gas oil to transit Iranian waters in order to evade an international inspection force.
U.S. complaints further charged Iranian smugglers with collecting a standard fee from the illegal activity.
The UN sanctions against Iraq imposed after Baghdad invaded Kuwait in 1990, forbid export of Iraqi oil and oil products, among other prohibitions.

The sanctions committee also was briefed on the status of implementing the oil-for-food accord. Panel members said there were no new developments, echoing previous UN statements about the status of the deal.
The last remaining issue for UN Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali relates to inspections to inspections by Dutch firm Saybolt of oil metering and pipeline equipment.
Committe members said the report by Saybolt will likely be submitted sometime this week, possibly allowing oil exports to start shortly thereafter.
